summary: Phase 2 accepts the reusable, deterministic dual-compiler harnesses. The harnesses now fail closed for resolution alias swapping, unreviewed parity exceptions, missing diagnostics, incompatible tsconfig postures, invalid resource records, nonzero benchmark exits, cache identity non-invalidation, ambiguous consumer ownership, out-of-manifest fixtures, and live process-group stop-loss cleanup.
evidence: Focused Phase 2 suite passed 9/9 in 31.045 seconds after the final fixture-startup remediation.
The live stop-loss fixture triggers the 80 percent RSS threshold and proves SIGTERM, exact five-second grace, SIGKILL, and verified reaping with no surviving non-zombie process-group members.

The all-39 tsconfig audit resolves local inheritance and records source-backed Node, Vitest, Jest, and Playwright ambient requirements; its deterministic matrix rejects CommonJS plus bundler plus ES5 and invalid interoperability.
Every consumer-matrix fixture and the runner must remain within the canonical fixture root, be declared by the exact SHA-256 manifest, and launch through shell-free argument vectors.

Review A passed independently. Review B passed source/security review; its terminal was unavailable, so root reran the dynamic focused suite and records that distinction in phase-2-review-b-result.json.
Python compilation, JSON parsing of review evidence, fixture manifest integrity, and git diff --check passed.
commands: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m py_compile measure/tests/test_typescript7_native_migration_phase2.py (PASS; generated bytecode removed)
next_phase_authorization: Phase 3 may begin only from an isolated branch rebased onto current master, whose synced pnpm lockfile fixes the stale Advantage Play Kit importer. Phase 3a is limited to root package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml, and captured install evidence; it must preserve the committed Codecamp manifest/lockfile pair.
